subject: MSA + Order Form: liability cap carve-outs for regulatory fines and third-party claims
messages:
From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-corp.com>, Acme Compliance <compliance@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines: liability cap exceptions for regulatory fines and 3rd-party claims

Hi Karthik,

Attached are Acme's latest redlines to the MSA and Order Form. Two items they flagged as non-starters on their side: (1) carve-outs from the liability cap for regulatory fines and statutory penalties (GDPR/CCPA exposure), and (2) carve-outs for third-party claims arising from data subject liabilities or payment card incidents (PCI).

They propose language that excludes "statutory fines and penalties" and "third-party claims arising from regulatory enforcement or PCI incidents" from the monetary cap, and that Redwood indemnify Acme for such claims.

Tom (procurement) asked if Redwood can accept these carve-outs or if we can offer a middle ground (e.g., an insurance-backed carve-out, a sub-cap, or a carve-out limited to willful misconduct). Please see the attached redlines and let me know Redwood's position and any workable counter-proposals.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Garcia
Senior Counsel, Acme Corporation
Attachment: Acme_MSA_redline_v3.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MSA redlines: liability cap exceptions for regulatory fines and 3rd-party claims

Laura / Rishi — forwarding Acme's redlines. Key asks summarized:
- Exclude regulatory fines/penalties from the aggregate liability cap (GDPR/CCPA, PCI).
- Exclude third-party claims (claims from customers/consumers or card brands) tied to regulatory enforcement or PCI events.

Marissa: Acme are pushing hard on this as a procurement condition before signing the Order Form. Can legal confirm whether we have flexibility to accept a limited carve-out or a sub-cap? Rishi — need your take on whether we should accept carve-outs for PCI/regulatory exposures or insist on retained risk/insurance.

Quick goal: propose a compromise we can live with that doesn't create unlimited exposure. My thoughts: limited sub-cap (e.g., up to 2x or 3x fees for regulatory fines), with requirement that Acme must pursue mitigation steps and that carve-out excludes negligence-only events. Thoughts?

-Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redlines: liability cap exceptions for regulatory fines and 3rd-party claims

Karthik — thanks for flagging. High-level legal view: we should avoid open-ended carve-outs that create uncapped exposure. Suggested positions (order of preference):

1) Reject unconditional exclusion of statutory fines from the cap. Offer instead a narrowly tailored exception only where fines directly result from Redwood's willful misconduct or proven gross negligence, and only up to a defined sub-cap (suggested: 3x annual fees, subject to insurance).

2) For PCI: require Acme to demonstrate that the PCI incident was caused by Redwood's validated failure to comply with our documented PCI controls. If accepted, apply a sub-cap tied to the affected contract value (e.g., amount paid in 12 months) and require prompt incident cooperation and remediation obligations from Acme.

3) Third-party claims: prefer to handle via indemnity limited to third-party claims where Redwood has a contractual indemnity (e.g., IP infringement). For regulatory enforcement actions, push back: regulators often seek statutory penalties and will sometimes go after the data controller (customer). We can agree to reasonable cooperation and contribution, but not blanket indemnity.

Practical ask: I need Rishi to review whether our compliance posture (SOC2, data handling, and PCI controls) supports an insurer-backed sub-cap or whether this creates unacceptably high residual risk. If insurance is available, we can offer a carve-out that is insured up to a threshold; otherwise we stick to willful misconduct + sub-cap.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redlines: liability cap exceptions for regulatory fines and 3rd-party claims

Laura / team — I reviewed the attached redlines and ran a quick risk estimate with Ops:
- GDPR/CCPA fines: severity depends on breach scope and culpability. For typical incidents, fines can be material, but our platform design (data segregation, tenant isolation, KV caching policies) reduces likelihood. However, in case of a root-cause due to a platform bug that exposed customer data, liability could be significant.
- PCI: we do not hold card PANs in plaintext; most customers use tokenization or third-party processors, but niche customers might flow card data through our runtime in supported integrations — risk remains.

Operational mitigation options: maintain documented PCI-compliant config list and require customers to opt into any direct card processing paths; provide mandatory secure-configuration checklists. If we contractually require customers to follow those steps, we reduce our exposure.

Insurance: I contacted our broker — cyber liability with regulatory fine coverage is available but comes at additional cost and limits. We could offer an insurer-backed carve-out up to a fixed cap (e.g., $2M) but would need Acme to acknowledge contributory failures and follow incident handling steps.

Recommendation: Accept a narrow regulatory carve-out only where Redwood's willful misconduct/gross negligence is established, OR offer insured sub-cap (Acme pays incremental premium or Redwood bundles it into the deal at a one-time fee). For PCI, require customer configuration obligations + sub-cap.

-Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@acme-corp.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: liability cap exceptions for regulatory fines and 3rd-party claims

Elena / Tom — thanks for the redlines and for the candid ask. We discussed internally and propose the following compromise we hope is acceptable to Acme: 

1) Regulatory fines/penalties (GDPR/CCPA/other statutory sanctions): not blanket excluded from the liability cap. Instead Redwood will accept an exception limited to cases of Redwood's proven willful misconduct or gross negligence, and only up to a defined sub-cap equal to 3x the annual fees paid under the Order Form, subject to available insurance coverage. If insurance is relied upon, parties will agree to a clearly scoped insurance endorsement.

2) PCI-related third-party claims: Redwood will not provide an unconditional indemnity. We will accept limited liability where the incident is caused by Redwood's failure to comply with our documented PCI configuration requirements. In such cases, liability will be limited to a sub-cap equal to the affected contract year's fees and contingent on Acme following incident response obligations (timely notification, preserve forensics, cooperation).

3) Third-party claims more generally: Redwood will continue to indemnify for IP infringement claims as standard. For regulatory enforcement actions brought against Acme by a regulator, Redwood will provide cooperation and contribution toward a negotiated settlement but will not agree to a broad indemnity for regulator-imposed statutory penalties absent willful misconduct.

If Acme is open to an insurer-backed sub-cap (we can scope a commercial proposal), we can document an explicit endorsement that covers regulatory fines up to the agreed threshold. Otherwise the willful-misconduct + sub-cap approach is our position.

Please let us know Acme's priority — (a) insured sub-cap, (b) sub-cap w/willful misconduct carveout, or (c) insist on full exclusion — and we will route accordingly. Happy to jump on a short call with your legal and procurement teams to close this quickly.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrderForm-Acme_Inc.xlsx
